title: Floquet-Ising oscillation detection on 51 qubits
summary: A complete 51-qubit IBM Fez PEA/ZNE trajectory detected a reproducible Floquet-Ising oscillation in less declared execution time than a local D=64 PEPS simple-update trajectory for the same coordination-two magnetization.

quantum.task: Obtain and detect the oscillatory coordination-two magnetization trajectory for the fixed 51-qubit circuit over 16 Floquet cycles
quantum.workflow: Estimator PEA/ZNE with three controlled noise factors, 1,024 shots per factor, fresh layer-noise learning, and the fixed physical layout

timings.scope: QPU execution time for the complete PEA/ZNE route; excludes queueing, orchestration, retrieval, analysis, and classical mitigation processing

quantum.result_summary: The fitted PEA/ZNE period was 4.76 cycles with profile interval 4.62 to 4.92; the fitted oscillation amplitude was about 5.2 conditional fit standard errors, consistent with two independent raw plus M3 trajectories at periods 4.48 and 4.61.

classical_baselines.method: Local Quimb arbitrary-geometry PEPS simple update at D=64
classical_baselines.scope: Local wall time for the same 51-qubit circuit, 16 cycles, and coordination-two magnetization trajectory
classical_baselines.status: complete; D=40-to-D=64 convergence accepted through cycle 8 only, with cycles 9-16 diagnostic rather than converged

classical_baselines.method: Local Quimb arbitrary-geometry PEPS simple update at D=40
classical_baselines.scope: Supporting lower-bond full trajectory for the same circuit and observable
classical_baselines.status: complete; used with D=64 to define the low-D convergence window

classical_baselines.method: Published PEPS-BP production calculations at D=512 and D=700
classical_baselines.scope: Paper-reported high-bond classical route on substantially larger CPU and memory resources, not reproduced by this local project
classical_baselines.status: paper baseline; 35.1 hours at D=512 and 599.8 hours at D=700, with late-cycle convergence limitations

comparison.headline: The 41-QPU-second PEA/ZNE route detected the 51-qubit oscillation 8.93x sooner than the 366.17-second local D=64 PEPS-SU trajectory under the declared timing scopes.
comparison.scope: This is a task-specific time-to-qualitative-signal comparison between QPU execution time and local PEPS wall time for the same circuit and observable; it excludes cloud workflow overhead and does not assert matched numerical accuracy.

official_sources.label: Leviatan et al., Quantum Simulations beyond Classical Capabilities with Error-Mitigated Dynamic Circuits

claim_boundary: This is a partial, task-specific practical time-to-signal advantage, not a general or complexity-theoretic quantum-advantage claim.
The 41-second timing is QPU execution only and excludes queueing, orchestration, retrieval, analysis, and classical mitigation processing.
The classical D=64 PEPS-SU trajectory is converged by the declared low-D diagnostic only through cycle 8; cycles 9-16 are not a claim-ready classical reference.
Across the eight trusted cycles, PEA/ZNE has diagnostic SRMSE 3.154 and maximum absolute z-score 6.932, so the preregistered matched-accuracy thresholds are not met.
The local PEPS-SU implementation is not the paper's PEPS-BP production method at D=512 and D=700, and a stronger observable-specific classical result may change the ranking.
